decision.summary: Five source-bounded competitor findings are suitable as reference expectations; broader customer and regional market claims remain uncurated.

findings.statement: NVIDIA's DGX B200 product page describes an eight-GPU data-center AI system; this establishes a system-level NVIDIA offer, not an apples-to-apples performance comparison with an accelerator product page.
Intel's current Gaudi documentation covers Gaudi 2 and Gaudi 3 and includes inference workflows for PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang.

IBM announced Intel Gaudi 3 availability on IBM Cloud in Frankfurt and Washington, D.C., with Dallas availability planned for Q2 2025; this is a partner-cloud deployment announcement, not proof of general availability in every region.
Broadcom identifies BCM78900 Tomahawk 5 as a 51.2 Tb/s StrataXGS Ethernet switch; this is networking evidence and does not by itself establish a complete inference system.

The reviewed official pages do not establish comparable United States or Europe transaction prices for complete NVIDIA, Intel, and Broadcom inference systems; a defensible comparison needs dated quotes with equivalent scope.
